column1: # Exact address-source audit: file, operation, expression, disposition, proof.
# Expressions are whitespace-normalized by machine_joints.py. No wildcard entries.
# ram = bounded WRAM (including documented mirrors); accessor = descriptor consumed by a named store seam;
# hardware = reverse DMA source field is a destination; the platform supplies the register read.

column5: send_a_part: FieldCallArgs.buffer is uint16_t; WORK_RAM_BANK=7E. The battlefield builder stages tiles/maps at MAP_BUFFER and passes their low words; no offset can change the bank.
clear_pixel: TILE_BUFFER_BANK=7E plus uint16_t row_at, then at most SECOND_PLANES=16 and the word high byte: 7E0000..7F0010, entirely WRAM, including the deliberate indexed overrun.
clear_pixel: TILE_BUFFER_BANK=7E plus uint16_t row_at, then at most SECOND_PLANES=16 and the word high byte: 7E0000..7F0010, entirely WRAM, including the deliberate indexed overrun.
tiles_of: TILE_BUFFER_BANK=7E OR uint16_t battle_object_tile_buffer (re/ram.toml); the dissolve consumes the tile buffer built for this combatant. No bank bits come from the offset.

stats_byte_at callers: effect_amounts.c at_block adds uint16_t block to STAT_WEAPON_ATTACK(+1), offsets below0x80. Direct slot callers use byte slot*0x80 plus fixed or byte-selected offsets<=0x1FF. stat_byte_by_place can pass an unrestricted uint16_t offset (stat_is keeps its stale high byte), but only when slot<BATTLE_COMBATANTS=11. With uint16_t battle_stat_block_place(0), the largest bound is0x7E0000+0xFFFF+10*0x80+0xFFFF=0x8004FE: banks7E/7F and bank80 low WRAM mirror only.
stray_place: battle_stat_block_place_stray returns uint16_t and offset is uint16_t; 7E0000 + FFFF + FFFF = 7FFFFE. Even stray combatant slots cannot leave the two WRAM banks.

line_effect callers supply only battle_line_tables[0..6] and battle_window_line_tables[frame&1], the declared re/ram.toml regions in bank 7E. point_the_line_effects and battle_show_window_table bound the indices; their indirect bank is also 7E.
stops_after_miss: MISREAD_BASE=7EB1F5, uint8_t tech<=255, PARTY_TECH_BYTES=11; highest byte 7EBCEA. This deliberately reads past the battle work table, but remains in bank 7E.

stray_box_place: uint16_t index<=FFFF added to 7EA039 or 7EA050 reaches at most 7FA04F, within the two WRAM banks. Producer leftover_index retains the original multiply result; no narrower table claim is made.

script_byte takes the wram_read8 arm only when bank==7E or bank==7F; script_operand masks the sum to 24 bits. Other banks use battle_animation_script_byte in script_data.h.
stray_status_byte explicitly casts the sum of the stat-block pointer and stat to uint16_t before OR with 7E0000. Even the original erroneous target index stays in WRAM.

QUEUE_BANK=7F OR uint16_t field_vram_queue_source/source2 (vars.h). field graphics builders queue offsets into the bank-7F sprite tile staging buffer. Offset cannot affect the bank.

TILE_MAP_BANK=7E OR uint16_t field_staged_line result/source; field_upload_layer_edge retains a uint16_t after each part, and field_send_bg3_piece selects FIELD_BG3. Staging regions are field layer edge buffers in re/ram.toml.

copy_sprite_tile takes this arm only for source_bank==FIELD_BUILD_BANK (7F); uint16_t from plus k<32 and word high byte reaches at most 80001E (bank80 low WRAM mirror). Other source banks use field_sprite_graphics_word.

repeat_line is called only by empty_outside_lines, which selects bank 7E/7F from column.bank&1. at is explicitly uint16_t on every iteration, so even a wrapped fill stays in that bank.
menu_send_loaded_graphics takes uint16_t from and fixes bank 7F. The menu loader unpacks its graphics there; no caller can supply bank bits in from.

upload_gate_rows has one caller, passing RAM_MENU_MODE7_PLANE=7F9000 as source. from preserves that bank and narrows the byte pick*row stride+source to uint16_t, so even stray row picks stay in 7F.

menu_put_glyph is called by typeset.c with menu_text_tiles: producers are field_window_staging (7EF000), battle_message_tiles, overworld_sign_label/menu_map_graphics, description TEXT_BANK=7E, or menu_set_label TILES_BANK=7E with a word offset. typeset tiles_are_writable bounds a line by LINE_REACH=0x1000. Even unguarded labels keep bank7E: first has a uint16_t low word, glyph_byte_place adds at most0x207, and the read column is pen/8<=31. The column-table audit found offsets<=0x5E0, so own<=7F07E6, still WRAM.

place_on_scene_edge is admitted by scene_edge_is_readable: bank must be 7E/7F and low-word table+selected edge offset+2<=10000. Its C object-command path uses the same state guard; re/ram.toml declares scene_window_edges as the window table pointer.
copy_map_tiles fixes MAP_BANK=7E; source low word is narrowed per row, i<across<=256. Maximum source+i=7F00FE. Map copying may overrun a row but cannot leave WRAM.
mark_entry fixes MAP_BANK=7E and table_entry returns uint16_t. The selector chooses the menu sprite/map table and wraps its entry arithmetic; bank cannot change.

This is operand-decoder metadata, not bytes: WORD_IN_BANK decodes command 33 into queue_upload, then menu_queue_object_upload; display.c send_object_queue consumes it through menu_upload_data (menu_data.h -> rom_data).
byte_at takes uint16_t address and fixes bank 7E for the out-of-slot fallback. In-slot reads use menu_object_slots accessors; both paths address work RAM.
move_label_right: left=7E0000+uint16_t sum, right=left+RIGHT_TILE=0x10. Thus 7E0000..7F000F, including wrap/overrun; producer is the save-screen label tile buffer.

save_run callers iterate eight menu_saved_run records from FFFA7B (menu_data.h; character records, inventory and event memory). The save-layout audit found five source banks are7E/7F and three are bank0 low-WRAM ranges (0100..010F,027E..027F,0290..02A0). in_bank preserves each run bank and narrows at+i; this reads the save source, while sv_write8 writes battery RAM.
ByteRef.at is uint16_t; cell_address adds it to 7E0000, so script cells always stay in bank 7E. The object arm uses typed menu object accessors.

group_record receives column from the 32-column map loops or last_map_tile (31); row_at is uint16_t. in_map_bank fixes 7E then adds at most31, maximum 7F001E, all WRAM.
tile_at takes uint16_t at, adds 7E0000; a word at FFFF reads its high byte at 7F0000, also WRAM. Tiles belong to the menu tilemap buffers.
copy_area narrows rows_down(source,r)+i to uint16_t before OR with 7E0000, so rectangle size cannot change the WRAM bank.
set_line_effect masks slot to 0..7 and narrows the table offset to uint16_t before OR with 7E0000. LINE_TABLES are the menu per-line workspace; indirect bank is also fixed 7E.

load_the_places starts at SCENE_STAGE=RAM_TILE_ANIMATION_TABLES=7F0400. Four fixed lists have byte counts<=255 and record sizes7,3,3,2; cursor advances at most 4+255*15=3830, ending below7F12F6. All count reads stay in unpacked WRAM.
text_byte fixes SCENE_LOWER_WORK_RAM=7E and takes uint16_t at. Captions/credits text is in the scene program unpacked at 7E3000; even a stray pointer stays in the bank.
scene_draw_circle constructs Circle.bank as 7E or7F from scene_circle_table_bank&1; in_table takes uint16_t. copy_line high byte can reach800000 only from7FFFFF, which is the bank80 low WRAM mirror.

widen_letters has one caller, passing NARROW_LETTERS (SCENE_UNPACK_BUFFER=7F0200); bank is its high byte and at wraps uint16_t for each row. The declared unpack buffer holds the decompressed two-plane letters.
page_list callers pass only PAGE_NAMES=7E6CAC or PAGE_JOBS=7E6CB6. Added index is explicitly uint16_t; including high byte reaches at most7F6CB6, still WRAM, even for a stray page.
text_byte fixes SCENE_LOWER_WORK_RAM=7E and takes uint16_t at. Captions/credits text is in the scene program unpacked at 7E3000; even a stray pointer stays in the bank.

scene_curtain_table_fits admits only FIRST_BANK=7E/SECOND_BANK=7F and bounds TABLE_REACH/HALVES_REACH. scene_curtain_stepped checks it before the C path, entry wrappers have the same guard. at narrows table+edges+line before OR.

This source is a uint16_t SceneScaling/PictureRequest bitmap offset, not a bus address. ask_for_picture -> picture_request -> scene_scaler_start stores it as scene_scaler_source_base; scaler.c pixel reads in fixed SCENE_UPPER_WORK_RAM=7F after bitmap_fits checks the sample extent.

scene_send_letters_widened callers in endings.c and planet.c set SCENE_UNPACK_BUFFER=7F0200 before unpacking letters. scene_unpacked_bank selects7F; 128 tiles*16 bytes end at7F09FF. The low word is not an unbounded index.
lay_out_mosaic bounds i<MOSAIC_TILES=0x140; MOSAIC_NUMBERS=7F2200 gives 7F2200..7F233F in the unpacked scene plane map.

credits_pieces is a fixed three-row table; every from is 7F0000 OR a constant word (CREDITS_PICTURE_AT, PATTERN_MAP, CREDITS_PATTERN_AT). send_a_credits_piece is called with the CreditsPiece enum; data were unpacked/built in that bank.
SCENE_UPPER_WORK_RAM=7F OR MosaicFrame.tiles, a uint16_t in the fixed mosaic_frames table. Frame selection indexes that table; its sizes and tile offsets refer to the built mosaic in WRAM.
packed_pixel_address masks SCENE_UNPACK_BUFFER+byte to17 bits then ORs7E0000. Result is exactly within7E0000..7FFFFF for every unsigned byte, not merely for the loader counts.
lay_out_the_panel starts attributes=SCENE_UNPACK_BUFFER=7F0200 and reads7 rows*32 attributes=224 bytes, ending7F02DF. The cockpit loader unpacks those attributes before this bounded loop.

word_past_the_list fixes SEARCH_BANK=7E with a 16-bit start offset; word<SEARCH_WORDS=0x8000, so adding2*word and the high byte reaches at most7FFFFE. Deliberate search beyond the declared task lists remains WRAM.
spread_the_pixels: PACKED_PIXELS=7E0C00 and n<packed, packed is uint16_t. Maximum read7F0BFE remains WRAM; the loader unpacks the packed pixels at that low-RAM address.
colour_at fixes SCENE_LOWER_WORK_RAM=7E and casts colours+2*i to uint16_t. step_the_colours and its leftovers use only that helper; a word high byte may enter7F0000, still WRAM.

read_descriptor consumes scene program data unpacked by boot.c from C31313 at7E3000. All ten caller tables (3D45,685E,7354,7B9C,7BB6,8FEA,9003,900E,9023,9029) encode bank7E for every entry; scene code updates their pointed-to values, not their bank bytes. d.table is uint16_t; both table and indirect data are7E.
